name: com.newonrecord/records
title: New on Record
description: Ohio's public records as their offices post them: bids, agendas, permits and more.

tools.name: list_kinds
tools.description: The kinds of record served, each with its JSON Schema and how many records and sources serve it. Not counted toward the daily limit.

tools.name: find_place
tools.description: Places whose name holds the words given, each with the id the other tools take as `place`. A county covers the places in it and its health district. With none, the note says which states the directory covers and how to ask for a place it doesn't hold. Not counted toward the daily limit.

tools.name: list_offices
tools.description: Which offices keep a kind of record for a place, and for each whether its records are served, or why not: not looked at by research, not online, kept by another office, not read, kept and held from serving, checked with nothing kept, a list of minutes alone, or served with none of the kind yet, each with the ask_for_data call that asks for it. Says what the directory holds, so a place it holds no file for reads as unknown, never as none. Each office's `outcome`: `not-looked`: Research hasn't looked yet for what the office posts of this kind, so what it keeps is unknown. `not-online`: The office posts none online (`instead` says what it does). `kept-elsewhere`: It says another office keeps them (`kept_by`). `not-read`: A source the checker doesn't read, holding no records of this kind (`not_read` says why). `held`: Its records of this kind are kept and not served (`not_read` says why). Where its terms bar us, `asked_on` is the day the registry records asking its office, or the company whose site it is, to allow them; it is null until then. `status-only`: Checked, with no record kept (`basis` says why). `minutes-only`: A list of its meetings' minutes alone, read for them (their kind is meeting.minutes) and holding none of this kind. `none-yet`: Its source is served and holds no records of this kind yet; the source's `status` and `cause` say why and what comes next. `served`: Its records are served. Where `not_read` is given, the checker no longer reads the source (since `since`) and serves what it read before. `no-source`: A keeper with no source of this kind in the directory. Beside it: `kept`, why it is in the answer: here (the place's own, or a place inside it), district (the place's health district, for a kind districts keep), body (an office another place says keeps its records), statewide (the state's or a federal office, for a kind no place keeps: search it with `source`). `named_by`, for `body`: the place whose entry names this office as its keeper. `instead`, for not-online and kept-elsewhere, what the office does instead (not-published, pdf-forms, request, another-body, …). For not-read and held, what would make the source readable. `via`, for a source whose records come through another: that source's id. `asked_on`, for held: the day the registry records its office, or the company whose site it is, was asked to allow it, as recorded once a send is; null until then, and for a source held for privacy. Not counted toward the daily limit.

tools.name: find_company
tools.description: Companies whose name starts with the words given, its ending (LLC, Inc.) aside, each with the id search_records takes as `company`, every way offices wrote its name, and its records by kind. A company is a name ending in LLC, Inc., Co. or another ending its state's law sets, so a person's own name is never one. At most 100 a page; pass next_cursor back for the next. Not counted toward the daily limit.

tools.name: get_company
tools.description: One company by its id (such as oh:certasite): every way offices wrote its name, and its records by kind, place and office. A link says only that offices wrote the same name: read each record's office and place. Not counted toward the daily limit.

tools.name: find_address
tools.description: One street address, written with its city (100 N Main St, Springfield) or as an id a record gave: its id, each way offices wrote it, and the served records there by kind, place and office. Records at one address are only at the same street address: a building holds many businesses. Not counted toward the daily limit.

tools.name: search_records
tools.description: Records by words, or filtered. With words (q), `order` is `best`, the best match first and the default, or `newest`; without words they come newest first. Records filtered by kind, place or source, a window of dates (ISO 8601 with a time zone), the office's own number, exactly (match, such as {"license_number": "12345"}: list_kinds names each kind's lookup fields), a state in our words (state, such as active or issued: list_kinds names each kind's), a company that names them (company, an id from find_company), or the street address they are at (address, an address's id: from find_address, or a record's address.id). A kind with a deadline, a bid's due date or a license's expiry, is found by when it passes (deadline_after, deadline_before, ISO 8601 with a time zone): deadline_after now gives the bids not yet due, whatever their status, which is the office's own word. A deadline the office gave as a date passes at that day's end. A kind whose records hold a city of their own, a carrier's or a license holder's, is found by it (city), and a carrier by its ZIP code (postal_code), across a statewide roster. Without words, records come newest first by `occurred_at`, the date each record's `dated_by` names. With words (q), every word must be in a record's text or the name it is filed under, in any order, and a word finds its other forms, never a word it is part of (HVAC* finds HVACR). Put "a phrase" in quotes, end a word with * for its beginning, start one with - to leave it out, and put OR between two words for either; AND and NOT are words like any other. Records then come best match first, or newest first with order=newest, each with `matched`: its values that hold the words. The page also gives `total` and `counts` by kind, place and year. Narrow by them rather than reading on: 10 to 20 a page is enough. limit=0 gives the counts alone, which count nothing against today's allowance. At most 100 a page; pass next_cursor back for the next. Each record returned counts against today's allowance.

tools.name: get_record
tools.description: One record by its id (`<source id>:<record id>`), with every stored version where the allowance includes history; with as_of (ISO 8601 with a time zone) too, the version first read at or before then, when the next was read, and the fingerprint of the page it was read from. An id the record had before it moved still finds it, returned under the id it has now. Counts as one record.

tools.name: list_changes
tools.description: What happened to records after a point, oldest first, each change with the record as it is now: new records, first listed by their source's nightly read (never history the checker read later), and where the allowance includes history, every change too (amended, status_change, closed, withdrawn; basis absent where a record left a list of what is in force). Start with since (ISO 8601 with a time zone), then pass back next_cursor to keep in step without missing one. Each change returned counts against today's allowance.

tools.name: ask_for_data
tools.description: Say what you were looking for and didn't find: a kind of record, a place, a source. The people who run the directory read every ask. Or name a record by its id where something about it seems wrong: the people who run the directory read it against its office's document, and what they find shows on the record. Not counted toward the daily limit.
